title: Chinese Hackers Use Fake Websites to Exploit Chrome and Windows Zero-Days
content_md: Chinese threat actors have expanded their use of a chained Chrome and Windows zero-day exploit kit, using convincing fake websites to target victims with malware. Volexity linked the latest activity to a third Chinese actor, tracked as UTA0565, which used spoofed media and policy websites during campaigns observed on September 3 and 4, 2026. The activity follows Volexity’s September 9 report on two other China-linked groups, UTA0560 and JungleBamboo, that used the same core exploit chain against selected targets. The chain abused Chrome vulnerabilities CVE-2026-85046 and CVE-2026-87491, followed by the Windows kernel local privilege-escalation flaw CVE-2026-85880. CVE-2026-85046 is a high-severity V8 type-confusion vulnerability that can allow code execution within Chrome’s sandbox through a crafted HTML page. Chinese Hackers Exploit Chrome Zero-Days UTA0565 used phishing emails with politically themed and organization-themed lures. One Chinese-language email urged recipients to support jailed Hong Kong activist Chow Hang-tung and oppose suppression of June 4 remembrance activities. Another campaign impersonated the Center for American Progress. Chinese Hackers Exploit Chrome Zero-Days (Source: volexity) The emails directed victims to attacker-controlled typosquatting domains designed to resemble legitimate websites.
